title: A New Method of Bone Stromal Cell Characterization by Flow Cytometry
protocol: Reconstitute murine long bones by partial digestion with collagenase I.
Isolate hindlimbs or forelimbs from mice for the procedure.
Combine hindlimbs and forelimbs to maximize cell yield.
Digest long bones to release 3‒6 × 10^6 cells per animal.
Isolate spines, forelimbs, and hindlimbs from five 28-week-old male mice.
Pool the samples after digestion.
Place materials in a laminar chemical hood or biosafety cabinet.
Prepare PBS containing 100 U/ml penicillin and 100 µg/ml streptomycin (PBS+P/S).
Prepare 1× PBS with 1 mM EDTA.
Dilute collagenase I to 1 mg/ml in PBS+P/S.
Prepare flow cytometry staining medium as per the recipe.
Dilute methanol-free formaldehyde to 1% concentration in PBS.
Dissect tissues under sterile conditions.
Incubate dissected tissues in collagenase solution at 37°C for approximately 30 minutes.
Pass digested tissue through a 40-µm cell strainer into a 50-ml conical tube.
Centrifuge the sample to pellet cells.
Resuspend cells in PBS+P/S and count using appropriate equipment.
Treat cells with methanol-free formaldehyde solution for fixation.
Wash cells in PBS+P/S after fixation.
Prepare samples for flow cytometry analysis.
Sacrifice mice according to an approved animal protocol.
Remove skin from the leg by cutting down the medial side and then removing skin with fingers to expose the entire limb musculature.
Remove hindlimb at hip joint, and place in PBS+P/S on ice.
Prepare a 10-ml syringe with PBS+P/S and attach a 27.5-G needle.
Place bones in a 100-mm dish.
Remove extra musculature and the foot with small surgical scissors and a scalpel using a 100-mm dish lid as a workspace.
Cut off proximal and distal ends of the long bones (tibia, femur, humerus).
Insert syringe containing PBS with 1 mM EDTA into the marrow cavity, and flush diaphysis with 2 to 3 ml PBS with 1 mM EDTA into a 50-ml tube.
Hold flushed bones with forceps, cut compact and trabecular bone into 1-to 3-mm chips with scissors.
Cut bones over a 15-ml conical tube to collect pieces and minimize debris.
Transfer bone chips into a 50-ml conical tube containing 1 to 3 ml of 1 mg/ml collagenase I in PBS+P/S.
Incubate the mixture 30 to 60 min at 37°C in a shaking incubator at 200 rpm (0.04 × g).
Combine partially digested bone chips with bone marrow extract.
Add PBS with 1 mM EDTA to achieve a final volume of 30 ml.
Mix cell suspension vigorously by pipetting 20 times or vortexing.
Filter cell suspension through a 40-µm cell strainer into a new 50-ml conical tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 min at 175 × g, room temperature.
Discard supernatant and resuspend in flow cytometry staining medium to an approximate concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells per ml.
Retrieve wrapped spine samples from −20°C.
Thaw samples for 36 hours in a tub at 4°C.
Unwrap spines in a biosafety hood.
Remove musculature and ligaments using a scalpel until intervertebral disc is revealed.
Using a bone saw, Dremel, or scalpel, remove vertebrae from the spine.
Irrigate the area with water if using a power tool to prevent aerosolization of bone.
Rewrap remaining spine in gauze covering the bone and keep on ice.
Return unwrapped portions to freezer when ready.
Using a Dremel and bone saw, remove spinal processes from vertebrae.
Using a Dremel and scalpel, remove intervertebral discs from both sides of vertebrae.
Cut a wedge into the vertebral body containing both cortical and trabecular bone using a Dremel and a bone saw.
Subdivide the cut wedge into 8 to 10 small pieces to expose as much surface area as possible for digestion.
Weigh the samples.
Place the weighed samples in 50-ml conical tubes with 10 ml of 3 mg/ml collagenase I in αMEM+P/S.
Incubate the sample in a 37°C shaking incubator overnight at 200 rpm (0.04 × g).
Strain sample through a 70-µm cell strainer.
Centrifuge for 3 to 5 min at 122 × g, room temperature.
Resuspend cells if additional debris is present and pass through the 70-µm cell strainer again.
Resuspend cells in 2 ml flow cytometry staining medium.
Sacrifice mice according to an approved animal protocol.
Do not use cervical dislocation when sacrificing, as it can injure the spine.
Open peritoneal cavity and remove organs to visualize the spine.
Cut on both sides of the spine from the base of the tail to the neck, ensuring ribs are also cut through.
Use a scalpel or scissors to clean off extra musculature and bones around the spinal process and spine.
When using spines from aged mice, handle with extra care as vertebrae can be fragile.
Remove ends of the spine near the brainstem and tail.
Store spines in cold PBS at 4°C for up to 1 week.
Cut remaining spine into three equal pieces using bone scissors.
Hold a spine piece vertically with forceps and cut open using scissors.
Move scissors horizontally and spread apart the sides of the spine to expose spinal cord.
Remove spinal cord from the spine piece.
Place remaining spine into a mortar with 10 ml cold PBS.
Crush spine pieces in mortar until liquid becomes pink.
Pipette fluid through a 40-µm cell strainer into a 50-ml conical tube.
Repeat steps of crushing and pipetting until PBS remains clear after crushing.
Centrifuge cell suspension for 5 min at 274 × g, room temperature.
Discard supernatant and resuspend cells in flow cytometry staining medium to an approximate concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells per ml.
Store samples at 4°C overnight if not staining immediately.
Store samples in 1% methanol-free formaldehyde in PBS for up to 2 weeks for long-term storage.
Fix cells in 1% methanol-free formaldehyde in PBS before or after staining for flow cytometry analysis.
Use unfixed cells for cell sorting.
Prepare fresh or fixed cells as required (see Basic Protocol 1, Alternate Protocols 1, and 2).
Stain cells with live/dead stain such as Zombie Aqua (BioLegend, cat. no. 423102).
Prepare flow cytometry staining medium according to the recipe provided.
Analyze stained cells by cell sorting or flow cytometry analysis.
Bring volume of fresh or fixed cells to 10 ml with PBS+P/S and mix thoroughly.
Take 10 µl sample, and combine with an equal volume of trypan blue.
Count cells with an automated cell counter (or using hemocytometer).
Dilute cells before counting as needed to ensure an accurate count.
Remove 1 × 106 cells per planned staining group.
Centrifuge the samples for 3 to 5 minutes at 122 × g at room temperature.
Prepare an unstained control sample.
Determine the negative population's location using the unstained control.
Assess autofluorescence with the unstained control.
For initial optimization, prepare fluorescence minus one (FMO) controls.
Prepare isotype controls for antibody titration.
Resuspend cells in PBS at 1 × 10^7 cells per ml.
Incubate cells with 1 µl live/dead staining solution per 1 ml cell solution for 20 min at room temperature.
Wash cells and resuspend in flow cytometry staining medium at 1 × 10^7 cells per ml.
Block samples with 5 µl appropriate FcR blocking solution per 10^7 cells for 30 min on ice.
Aliquot 100 µl samples into each staining group, including unstained control, into 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tubes or 96-well plates.
Stain with primary antibody for 30 min on ice in the dark.
Wash cells and centrifuge for 5 min at 175 × g if secondary antibody staining is required.
Repeat steps of staining with primary antibody with the secondary antibody.
Wash twice in flow cytometry staining medium, centrifuging for 5 min at 175 × g at room temperature.
Resuspend cells in a flow cytometry tube containing 100 µl cell sorting buffer for cell sorting.
Resuspend sample in 100 µl of 1% methanol-free formaldehyde in PBS (1 × 10^6 cells per 100 µl) while mixing to prevent clumping, and move to flow cytometry tube for analysis.
Store covered in foil at 4°C until ready to run cell sorting or flow cytometry analysis.
Store samples for up to 24 hours before cell sorting.
Store samples for up to one week before flow cytometry analysis.
Run single color compensation controls with each experiment.
Determine autofluorescence using an unstained control.
Perform antibody titration to find the optimal staining concentration.
Conduct FMO controls to assess proper gating of positive cell populations.
Analyze fixed and unfixed cells representative of those being analyzed in experiments.
Prepare and stain cells according to Basic Protocol 2.
Add groups for FMO analysis, isotype controls, and antibody titration.
Prepare antibody dilutions as described in Table 5 for murine samples and Table 6 for primate samples at 25%, 50%, 100%, and 200% of manufacturer-recommended volume.
Test approximate concentrations within a smaller range once chosen.
Set up staining groups as shown in Table 7 for murine samples and Table 8 for primate samples.
Create mixes for each staining group, excluding a single antibody.
Conduct a flow cytometry minimal overlap control panel to identify fluorochrome bleed over with cell-specific antibody mixes.
Confirm no fluorochrome bleed over into the fluorescence minus one channel.
Conduct a fluorescence-minus-one (FMO) control panel to identify fluorochrome bleed over with cell-specific antibody mixes.
Set up staining groups for isotype controls as shown in Table 9 and Table 10 for murine and primate samples, respectively.
Run isotype controls with each new experimental cohort.
Mix PE rat IgG2a with samples as an isotype control.
Mix APC rat IgG1 with samples as an isotype control.
Mix PerCP-Cy5.5 rat IgG2b with samples as an isotype control.
Mix PE hamster IgG with samples as an isotype control.
Mix APC rat IgG2b with samples as an isotype control.
Mix FITC rat IgG2a with samples as an isotype control.
Mix FITC rat IgG2b with samples as an isotype control.
Mix PerCP-Cy5.5 mouse IgG2b with samples as an isotype control.
Mix PE mouse IgG2b with samples as an isotype control.
Mix FITC mouse IgG1 with samples as an isotype control.
Mix APC mouse IgG1 with samples as an isotype control.
Use isotype controls to determine nonspecific background contribution and correct for nonspecific binding.
Take samples and prepared compensation beads on ice to the cell sorting facility.
Prepare collection tubes with 2 ml of cell sorting buffer.
Prepare side scatter (SSC) and forward scatter (FSC) gates based on unstained controls.
Set photomultiplier tube (PMT) voltages according to procedures outlined in Maecker & Trotter (2006).
Run compensation beads and live/dead controls to generate a compensation matrix.
Use beads to adjust FSC and SSC.
Name all parameters for consistency between experiments.
Run a single-stained bead sample to ensure positive peaks are on scale.
Do not record data until all beads are reviewed and on the scale.
Rerun single-stained bead samples to perform compensation setup.
Record files for compensation controls.
Set a gate around the SSC height (SSC-H) versus FSC height (FSC-H) scatter to remove debris.
Set a gate around the singlet population using FSC-H versus FSC-A.
Use the singlet population gate for further analysis.
Gate live, Zombie Aqua (AmCyan channel) negative cells.
Within the live, singlet population gated above, for murine samples, gate on the Sca1 high and CD34 high population.
For primate samples, gate the CD45 high and CD34 high population.
Gate on the Sca1 high and CD29 high population within the live, singlet population for murine samples.
Gate the CD90 high and CD146 high population after gating on the Sca1 high and CD29 high population for murine samples.
Gate on the CD146 high and CD90 high population within the live, singlet population for primate samples.
Gate the CD146 high and CD29 high population after gating on the CD146 high and CD90 high population for primate samples.
Gate on the alkaline phosphatase high and CD90 high population within the live, singlet population for murine samples.
Gate on the alkaline phosphatase high and CD90 high population within the live, singlet population for primate samples.
Gate on the SPARC high and podoplanin high population within the live, singlet population.
For murine samples, gate on the CD11b high and CD68 high population followed by gating on the CD265 low and CD115 low population.
For primate samples, gate on the CD11b high and CD68 high population followed by gating on the CD254 low and CD115 low population.
Gate on the CD68 high and CD115 high population within the live, singlet population for murine samples.
Follow up by gating on the CD11b low and CD265 high population to identify osteoclasts in murine samples.
For primate samples, gate on the CD68 high and CD115 high population within the live, singlet population.
Follow up by gating on the CD11b low and CD254 high population to identify osteoclasts in primate samples.
Run samples according to the sorter's manufacturer's protocol.
Place sorted samples on ice for downstream experiments.
Retain sorting reports with cell counts and percentage of stained cell data.
Run compensation beads to generate a compensation matrix.

Ensure an SSM of 0 to 5 is great and 6 to 9 is acceptable; adjust voltage gains if above 10.
Desire 3 to 4 median channel logs between the peaks for positive and negative separation, but use fewer for markers with lower expression.
Run live/dead controls if samples were created with unfixed cells during staining.
Generate unstained gating controls for SSC and FSC using unstained samples.

Calculate cell percentages or mean fluorescence intensities using analysis software.
Graph to profile changes in the numbers of bone marrow-residing cells.
Prepare compensation beads for cell sorting and flow cytometry.
Mix antibodies of interest with flow cytometry staining medium according to protocol.
Vigorously mix beads by inverting at least 10 times or pulse vortexing.
Add one drop of beads to each tube or well.
Add 2 μl of each antibody in 2 ml flow cytometry staining medium.
Mix well by inversion or pulse vortexing.
Incubate at 4°C for 30 min in the dark.
Add 2 ml flow cytometry staining medium to each tube.
Centrifuge 5 min at 400 × g, 4°C.
Remove supernatant and add 400 μl flow cytometry staining medium to each sample.
Vortex prior to running sample.
